# KaPin

> KaPin is a free, open-source (MIT) screenshot toolkit for Linux X11 desktops. Written in Python with PyQt5, it bundles region/window capture, in-place annotation, automatic scrolling long screenshots, Tesseract-based Chinese & English OCR, pin-to-screen images, and screen recording (MP4/GIF/MKV) into a single tray app.

## What KaPin does

- **Region capture**: drag a box, resize with eight handles and a pixel loupe, then annotate immediately in place — no separate editor window in the way.
- **Window capture**: click a window to capture it whole.
- **Annotation**: rectangle, ellipse, arrow (four head styles), line (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot), pen, text, numbered steps, highlight with adjustable opacity, spotlight (dims the picture around a region you choose), blur/mosaic (to hide sensitive info) with adjustable intensity, magnifier, crop — with adjustable color and line width, undo/redo, and double-click to edit text on the canvas.
- **OCR text recognition**: Tesseract-powered, recognizes Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English; runs automatically when a capture opens in the editor, supports drag-selecting words on an image, and can grab text from a screen region straight to the clipboard. Layout modes and image enhancement improve accuracy.
- **Scrolling long screenshot (auto)**: KaPin auto-scrolls a target window and stitches frames into one tall, seamless image — ideal for web pages, chat logs, code, and documents.
- **Scrolling long screenshot (manual)**: the user scrolls and KaPin stitches, with a live preview that skips rows already captured.
- **Pin to screen**: keep images floating on top (drag to move, scroll to zoom, Ctrl+scroll for opacity, double-click to close); pins are themselves annotatable and their recognized text is drag-selectable.
- **Screen recording**: a toolbar beside the selection sets frame rate, resolution, countdown, and duration; export to MP4, GIF, or MKV with progress and repeat exports.
- **Save annotated images**: keep the original image size while preserving annotations, as PNG or JPEG.
- **Workflow**: global keyboard shortcuts, system tray, single instance, configurable save folder and filename template, auto-copy/auto-save, restart-surviving history, accent themes, and a bilingual Chinese/English UI.

## Who it is for

Linux X11 users who want one good, self-contained screenshot solution — capture, annotate in place, OCR, and pin references to the screen. KaPin is one of the few Linux scrolling-screenshot tools with built-in OCR.

## Requirements

- An X11 session (`echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE` returns `x11`). Wayland is not supported because simulated scrolling and full-screen grabbing are restricted there.
- System packages (apt): tesseract-ocr, tesseract-ocr-chi-sim, tesseract-ocr-chi-tra, fonts-noto-cjk, ffmpeg.
- Python packages (in a venv): PyQt5, mss, opencv-python-headless, numpy, pillow, pynput, pytesseract.

## Install and run

- Install: `git clone https://github.com/CyberAn-Dev/KaPin.git && cd KaPin && bash install.sh`
- Run: launch "KaPin" from the application menu, or run `./run.sh`. The deb package name and command remain `kapture`.
- Direct actions: `./run.sh --region`, `--window`, `--scroll`, `--manual`, `--color`, `--record`, `--pin1`.
